trust_decision.summary: miniserv decides which parts of a request line are secret and must be masked before the access log is written; the decision is a single regex in sanitise_logged_request (request-line shape + [?&;]name= match), and separately login_redirect hands the plaintext password to an external program on its argv.

landing_point.why: summary says 'information disclosure via regex pattern' (CWE-185/777); the only redaction regex in the web server is the request-line/param regex in sanitise_logged_request.

fix_sites.entry_point: any HTTP request to miniserv that is access-logged (log_request callers, e.g. miniserv.pl:2519, miniserv.pl:2944)

fix_sites.module_kind: core web server, login redirect helper (external program call)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: miniserv.pl:5009 (login_redirect builds a shell command with the password as an argv element; distinct from the log sanitiser at miniserv.pl:3442)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: login_redirect is an admin-configured hook that is not exposed in the UI and is documented as receiving the password, so a solver can argue argv exposure is intended behaviour, not part of a log-redaction regex bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: non-sensitive query parameters (e.g. page=, user=, xnavigation=) and the method/path/HTTP version must still be logged verbatim; nolog matching uses the unsanitised request (request_nolog) and must keep working; masking everything or dropping the line breaks log analysis and nolog filters.

O7_producer.where: miniserv.pl:3425-3438 (default list plus log_redact_params from miniserv.conf)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Referer and other headers logged via logheaders/logclf are written raw, so a Referer carrying ?password=... bypasses the request-line redaction
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: headers are a neighbouring feature (CLF/logheaders option), not the request line the sanitiser was written for

O8_uncovered_routes.route: request lines that the sanitiser's shape regex does not match (URI containing whitespace, accepted by the parser's (.*) at miniserv.pl:1425, or non-HTTP/x.y lines logged via http_error 400) are logged with no redaction at all
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: malformed / unusual request lines look like an unsupported combination
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: parser differential between miniserv.pl:1425 and miniserv.pl:3451, ~2000 lines apart

O8_uncovered_routes.route: parameter-name spellings the [?&;]name= match misses: percent-encoded names, array/suffixed names (pass[]=, user_password=), and names nested inside an encoded page= value from the login redirect (page=%2Fx%3Fpass%3D...)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: encoded or nested names are not literally the configured parameter name
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same line as landing point; login-redirect producer at miniserv.pl:2166-2171

O8_uncovered_routes.route: debug log writes the raw request line and plaintext passwords
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: debug logging is opt-in and developer-only

O8b_injection_room.sibling: run_login_script passes the new session id on argv like login_redirect passes the password
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same quotemeta-and-shell pattern used for all hook scripts; a maintainer adding a password arg to the login hook would copy it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: header logging path applying its own (weaker) masking for Authorization/Cookie
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: logheaders lets admins log arbitrary headers; a second redaction implementation there is a natural addition

O9_family: information disclosure: incomplete secret redaction in logs / secret on process argv (regex-based sanitiser, CWE-185/777)
